title: The Multisig Registry records only three fields and currently contains no entries
content:
A.2.11.1.3.4.1 defines the registry entry as three fields: "Multisig Name," "Administrator Entity," "Multisig Address." A.2.11.1.3.4.2.0.6.1 renders the table with a single blank row — no multisigs are registered.

The field list is narrower than the registration process that feeds it. A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.8 requires the administrator to supply the Impact Classification and Operational Classification to Core GovOps as part of registration, and A.2.11.1.3.3.1.1 makes reviewers verify "that Multisig documentation in the Multisig Registry remains accurate." But classification is not among the three recorded fields, so the artifact that reviewers check does not carry the data that determines what compliance means for that multisig. Either the classifications live somewhere unnamed, or the registry is thinner than the framework it supports.

The empty table is less alarming than it looks: A.2.11.1.3.2 states that these requirements "shall take effect on May 20, 2026," and both the monitoring and enforcement provisions repeat that they "apply only after the effective date." This is a framework published ahead of activation, not one being ignored.

The consequence worth tracking is the transition. Registration is a precondition for inclusion in any Spell, and multisigs "currently in use" are in scope — so on the effective date, an unpopulated registry and a live set of operating multisigs must be reconciled, with a 48-hour enforcement clock waiting behind it.
description: Registration collects impact and operational classifications, but the registry stores only name, administrator entity and address — and its table is empty ahead of the May 2026 effective date.
